newsitem.title: JAPAN: Green Cross pays penalties for tax evasion.
newsitem.headline: Green Cross pays penalties for tax evasion.

text.p: Green Cross Corp said on Tuesday that the Osaka Regional Taxation Bureau had imposed financial penalties and back-taxes on the pharmaceutical firm for unreported income over a three-year period.
"We have followed the taxation authority's decision and paid penalties and back-taxes," a company spokesman said. However, he declined to comment on the amounts involved.
Media reports said that the Osaka tax bureau had imposed 90 million yen in penalties and back-taxes against the Osaka-based drugs firm for evading taxes on about 200 million yen in unreported income.
The spokesman said that the Osaka tax bureau had conducted an examination of the company for the period from 1990 to 1992.
He said that the tax authority had characterised certain expenditure, which the company listed under research and other non-taxable items, as entertainment.

Green Cross has been at the centre of a scandal over HIV-tainted blood products. Japanese prosecutors last week indicted three former presidents of the company on charges of professional negligence resulting in deaths from the sale of HIV-contaminated blood products.
